# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**Best overall: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-$150)**
- It's the top pick at What Hi-Fi, Best Products, and iTechGuides.
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (up to 28 with Playtime Boost), and a removable handle, and it can charge your phone.
- Prices at What Hi-Fi were $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon.
- Buy links: [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Best for pool parties: Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM**
- Tom's Guide ranks it best overall, and RTINGS names it best mid-range.
- It has an IP67 rating, floats, and plays 360-degree sound, so it sounds the same wherever you sit.
- Its battery lasts about 15 hours.
- Buy links: [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)

**Best budget: Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 (about $65-$80)**
- It's softball-sized, IP67, and floats, with about 14 hours of battery.
- It's quieter and has less bass than the bigger models.
- Buy links: [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/), [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**Best for loud, big gatherings: JBL Boombox 4**
- RTINGS' top overall pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and lasts over 40 hours.
- It's heavy and pricey, and the sound is narrow, so it can get muffled if you're beside or behind it.
- Buy link: [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- A similar option is the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus (100 W, IPX7, floats, 3.8 kg). It lists at $249.99, or $200 with code AFSC20 per Dealectric. I found no independent review of it. This is an affiliate link: [Soundcore via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus)

**Easy to carry**
- **JBL Grip (about $100):** Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, can-shaped, and under a pound, with 12 hours of battery. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **JBL Go 5 (about $40):** The best budget pocket speaker at What Hi-Fi, with IP67 but only 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

**Tips**
- Look for IP67 or higher for a pool. For sand, make sure the first number is 5 or 6, since the Boom 2 has no dust rating.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use if the manufacturer allows it, and dry the charging port before plugging in (RTINGS, iTechGuides).
- Keep it on a towel rather than buried in sand, and out of direct sun.
- If you'll be in the water, choose one that floats, such as the EPICBOOM, WONDERBOOM 4, or Boombox 4.

I couldn't open the retailer pages directly, so the links above go to the reviews, which have current price and buy buttons. Check the price before you buy.
